objective: Deciding who stays accountable when the Product Owner delegates Product Backlog work
secondaryObjectives: Assigning the Product Owner's accountabilities for value and the Product Backlog, and why the Product Owner is one person
Organizing several Scrum Teams on one product around one Product Backlog, one Product Owner and one Product Goal

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Daily Scrum: 'The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary'; 'a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team'. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's sprint-status-meeting-daily-scrum (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The company, the product, the team and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master of two Scrum Teams building Alderbank Insurance's claims app, a fictional insurer. The Product Owner, Priya, is moving to a part-time role for two months and has asked a business analyst to 'own the backlog'. A second team joined last month with its own backlog.
handover: Priya will still attend Sprint Reviews. The analyst, Marco, is skilled at refinement.
Team B keeps a separate backlog in a spreadsheet; both teams build features of the same app.
howItWorks: The board shows the Sprint's commitments, the work, the impediments, the people's support and the Scrum events.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each Daily Scrum; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

backlogs.label: Look at both teams' backlogs
backlogs.available: not busy and phase == "run" and isNull(backlogsAt)
backlogs.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.finding: Two backlogs order the same app's work differently; Team B is building a settlement screen Team A's ordering puts last.

ask.label: Ask Priya what she wants Marco to do
ask.available: not busy and phase == "run" and isNull(askAt)
ask.why: Done, or finish what you are doing first.

effects.finding: Priya wants Marco to write and refine items; she assumed he would also decide the order and accept work.

options.label: Priya accountable while Marco does delegated work, one Product Backlog for both teams, and the Definition of Done held

then.log: Day 2: Marco reorders the backlog around a stakeholder's request; Priya reverses it at the Review; the teams lose two days of work.
Day 3: Team B ships a settlement screen nobody asked for this quarter; the photo upload the Sprint Goal needs is behind.
Day 4: screen-reader users can't upload claim photos; complaints reach the regulator's accessibility office.

effects.log: Day 3: a stakeholder asks Marco to accept a half-done feature.

delegPrompt.title: Who owns the backlog now?
delegPrompt.context: Marco will refine items; Priya is part-time.

choices.label: Marco may refine and write items, but Priya stays accountable for ordering and value; make that transparent to both teams and stakeholders

effects.log: The team hears that Priya remains accountable.

choices.feedback: The Product Owner may delegate work but remains accountable (Scrum Guide 2020).

choices.label: Let Marco and Priya work it out between them
choices.feedback: Ambiguity means the team guesses who decides.

choices.label: Tell the teams Marco is the Product Owner now and decides the order

effects.log: Marco is announced as Product Owner.

choices.feedback: The Product Owner is one accountable person; transferring it informally leaves nobody with authority.

oneblPrompt.title: Two teams, two backlogs
oneblPrompt.context: Team B's spreadsheet backlog conflicts with Team A's.

choices.label: Help Priya merge into one Product Backlog she orders, with one Product Goal, refined jointly by both teams
choices.feedback: Several Scrum Teams on one product share one Product Backlog, one Product Owner and one Product Goal.

choices.label: Keep two backlogs and hold a weekly sync
choices.feedback: It reduces conflict but two orders still compete.

choices.label: Let Team B keep its own backlog and priorities
choices.feedback: Two teams optimize two orders for one product.

acceptPrompt.title: Marco is asked to approve undone work
acceptPrompt.context: The photo upload works but fails the accessibility check in the Definition of Done.

choices.label: Explain that the Definition of Done decides what is done; the item returns to the Product Backlog and Priya is told

effects.log: The undone item stays out of the Increment.

choices.feedback: An item that doesn't meet the Definition of Done can't be released or presented as done.

choices.label: Ask Priya to decide at the Review
choices.feedback: Better than accepting it, but the Definition of Done isn't the Product Owner's to waive.

choices.label: Let Marco accept it as done to keep the stakeholder happy
choices.feedback: Releasing undone work hides it from everyone and breaks the Definition of Done.

reflection.question: Write a note to the teams and stakeholders: who is accountable for the Product Backlog during Priya's part-time months, how the two teams now work, and why the photo upload wasn't released.

parts.label: Accountability
parts.criteria: Priya remains accountable; Marco does delegated refinement; one backlog and one Product Goal for both teams.
parts.modelAnswer: Priya stays accountable for value and the order of the one Product Backlog both teams share; Marco helps refine it.

parts.label: Done
parts.criteria: The Definition of Done decides; undone work returns to the backlog.
parts.modelAnswer: The upload failed the accessibility check in our Definition of Done, so it went back to the backlog.

source.note: Nothing undone released or presented as done (Scrum Guide 2020).
Every team and stakeholder gauge at 60 of 100 or more at the end.

scoring.modelReasoning: The Product Owner may delegate Product Backlog work to others but remains accountable for it, and is one person, not a committee. Several Scrum Teams on one product share one Product Backlog, one Product Owner and one Product Goal. The Definition of Done is the commitment for the Increment: work that doesn't meet it isn't released or presented as done, whoever asks.
